content.text: {"label":"sick_wave","explanation":"Staffing is short on both queues (payments 52 vs 61.4 expected, -15%; general 47 vs 57.6, -18%). Attendance shows 12 sick absences on payments and 13 on general, against about 2.4–2.6 usually. Most are noted as 'Called in sick - fever' and were logged between 07:00 and 15:00. Demand is not the driver: today's volume is 2% under forecast on payments and 4.5% under on general. Average handle time is close to forecast. The only open incident is a P4 branch printer fault with branch-only impact, and there are no marketing entries. General shows a mild balance_enquiry rise (1.48x normal), but overall general volume is on forecast and already covered by chat deflection. The cause is a supply shortfall from an illness wave.","plan_name":"No further intraday action – day closed","rationale":"It is now 20:00, the end of the operating window, so no time remains to apply any lever. The last hour also recovered: payments service level was 84–100% from 18:45 onward, and general was 97–100%. The levers already used (coaching cancellations, overtime, break delay, chat deflection, callback) covered the gap. Further offers would add cost with no benefit. Recommendation for tomorrow: check attendance early, since fever cases often run several days. Pre-plan overtime and coaching cancellations from the start of day, but keep within the Rs 15,000 daily overtime budget.","actions":[]}
